correctness.rationale: For independent A,L~Exp(lambda) the probability a single window [s,s+w] intersects [A,A+L) equals exp(-lambda*s)*(lambda*s+1-exp(-lambda*w)). Disjoint first-interception events exactly sum as exp(-lambda*T_previous)*F(g_i,w). Dynamic programming reduces every gap to e^(-y)[y+1-x+x*v], with unique maximizer y=x(1-v) and optimum exp[-x(1-v)]. Induction yields the unique calendar and all-n value. The increasing Bellman values force strictly increasing chronological gaps. epsilon_(n+1)=1-exp(-x epsilon_n) has a positive infinite product epsilon_n/x^n for 0<x<1 because sum epsilon_n converges; at x=1 its inverse increment tends to 1/2, proving n epsilon_n ->2. The cumulative gap bound follows by a geometric majorant. The extracted standard-library checker passed 16596 tests including direct overlap quadrature and perturbed/random alternative calendars. It is finite supplementary evidence, not the proof.

value.rationale: For a fixed number and duration of intermittent survey windows on a one-time transient ecological episode, a unique all-size nonperiodic calendar with strictly increasing gaps is a concrete design invariant. The exact positive infinite-product factor 0<C(x)<1 quantifies the benefit of separating windows compared with uninterrupted observation from time zero with the same active effort. The sharp x=1 snapshot algebraic n^-1 miss law versus every fixed x<1 exponential x^n law, with bounded versus logarithmically divergent total idle time, supplies a substantive structural boundary and motivates the exact calculation. It is not a claim about empirical eDNA performance, and the strong perfect-overlap assumption is explicitly bounded.
